title.narrative: Sector Support for Education Reform Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to create conditions for improved learning outcomes in basic education.

The objective of the Sector Support for Education Reform Project for Kyrgyz Republic is to create conditions for improved learning outcomes in basic education. There are three components of the project, the first being enhanced learning. This component has following four sub-components: (1) improving pedagogical practices to finance the design and implementation of an in-service training program for about ten thousand primary school teachers to improve teaching-learning practices in support of the newly revised curriculum. It will also finance a training program designed to enhance the capacities of approximately one thousand five hundred Deputy Directors, district level methodologists and inspectors to support primary level teachers to teach the new curriculum; (2) resources for learning to finance the design, printing and distribution of approximately three million textbooks, teacher guides and student workbooks for primary and lower secondary schools, and a package of essential teaching-learning materials for primary schools; (3) supporting ongoing revision of curriculum for grades five-nine focusing on the piloting and finalization of subject standards and program content; and (4) assessment of learning to finance a sample-based survey of student learning achievements at grade four, and assessments of teaching-learning practices at the primary level. The second component being improved management and accountability of school resources. This component has following two sub-components: (1) improving financial management for financing the design and operationalization of a monitoring system for school budgets and expenditures, training and technical assistance to key players at the local and central level; and (2) strengthening school leadership and management to finance training of school directors and accountants. The last component is communications and implementation support. This component has following two sub-components: (1) communications and outreach activities to finance activities to engage and inform stakeholders about the changes in the education sector; and (2) implementation support to finance project operating costs, including inter-alia translation, interpretation, equipment, supervision costs, salaries of the staff in the project coordinating unit, and incremental operating costs at the Ministry of Education and Science.

condition.narrative: Finance Agreement :B-1-(b) | Description :No withdrawal shall be made for payments for Category (2) of the Eligible Expendituresdisbursement category until the GoK has adopted a sustainable financing mechanism acceptable to the Bank to ensure timelyreplacement of textbooks for all grades of general basic education.

title.narrative: Percentage of students in grades 3-4 using a revised textbook for Mother-Tongue Language, Mathematics and Motherland Studies.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The indicator exceeded its target value.</strong> By the project completion, 100 percent of students in Grades 3-4 received and were using revised textbooks for Mathematics, Mother-tongue Language and Motherland Studies, thus exceeding the end-of-project target of 85 percent by 15 percentage points for these textbooks.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of schools that received revised textbooks for Mathematics, Mother-tongue, and Natural Sciences for Grade 5.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target was achieved.</strong> All schools in the country were provided with revised Grade 5 textbooks for Mathematics, Mother-tongue, and Natural Sciences.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of schools that received revised textbooks in Mother-tongue, Mathematics and Motherland Studies for Grade 4.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target was achieved</strong>. Textbooks for Mathematics, Mother-tongue and Motherland Studies were provided to 100 percent of schools.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of schools that received revised textbooks in Mother-tongue, Mathematics and Motherland Studies for Grade 3.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target was achieved</strong>. Textbooks for Mathematics, Mother-tongue and Motherland Studies were provided to 100 percent of schools.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of primary schools that received a package of essential teaching-learning materials.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target was achieved</strong>. All primary schools in the country were supplied with packages of essential teaching-learning materials including digital content for primary and secondary grades.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of schools that received revised textbooks for Mathematics, Mother-tongue, and Natural Sciences for Grade 6.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target was achieved</strong>. All schools in the country were provided with revised Grade 6 textbooks for Mathematics, Mother-tongue, and Natural Sciences.</p>

title.narrative: Number of additional qualified primary teachers resulting from project interventions.

comment.narrative: <p> <strong>The target was exceeded</strong>. The Project trained 10,043 primary school teachers and 1,746 deputy directors. <strong>???????</strong></p>

title.narrative: Total number of 5th and 6th grade textbook manuscripts approved by MoES.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target was exceeded</strong>. By completion, the new curriculum-aligned manuscripts were developed, piloted and revised for 37 subjects in Grades 5 and 6.</p>

<p><strong>Both targets were exceeded. </strong>By completion, the project benefitted 467,444 people, including:  (i) 11,789 teachers, school directors, deputy directors and school accountants, RED methodologists and RED accountants; (ii) 237,925 Grade 3-4 students; and (iii) 214,562 Grade 5-6 students. The number of female beneficiaries who benefited from project interventions exceeded the end-of-project target by 19 percentage points and can be explained by the fact that majority of teacher workforce are females.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of training-certified primary grade teachers who follow the revised curriculum and apply improved teaching-learning practices in Mother-tongue Language and Mathematics.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target was exceeded. </strong>69 percent of training-certified teachers reported that they applied improved teaching-learning skills in the beneficiary survey conducted by the third party. Further analysis conducted with the CLASS data defined the improvement in practice in qualitative terms and the result demonstrated that 59 percent of the training-certified teacher have improved their practice. <strong> </strong></p>

title.narrative: Percentage of schools where Per Capita Financing (PCF) is introduced starting in year 2012 or later that post the annual school budget and expenditures report.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target was exceeded</strong>. Out of 95 percent of schools operating under the PCF modality 78.8 percent post their annual school budget and expenditure reports, as part of the digitized School Report Cards.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of schools where Per Capita Financing (PCF) was introduced starting in 2012/13 or later that annually produce a School Report Card.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target was exceeded</strong>. A total of 95 percent of schools in the country that prepare their budgets in compliance with the PCF also produce SRCs in accordance with the order of the MoES “On organizational measures to implement the school reporting system under the Education Management Information System."</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of school directors and AO Heads and accountants who are certified as having successfully completed the course financed under the Project.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target was exceeded</strong>. A total of 2,091 school directors were trained in school leadership, development planning, engaging stakeholders for community participation, budget formation, expenditure monitoring and reporting under PCF; 422 RED and school accountants, plus 85 RED specialists were trained on the general concepts of the PCF and its governing regulations, on how to estimate school income, and on the basics of accounting for schools and expenditures monitoring under PCF.</p>

title.narrative: Gender Parity Index for Primary Gross Enrollment Ratio.

comment.narrative:
<p>The project Gender Parity Index value, at 0.95 with a statistical difference of 0.05, is only slightly below the threshold value of 0.97 and requires trend analysis for any future targeted interventions.</p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: System for learning assessment at the primary level

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Both targets were achieved</strong>. The Project  contributed to strengthening the system for learning assessment at the primary level by carrying out a fourth round of NSBA in 2017 (previous rounds of NSBA were conducted in 2007, 2009 and 2014).</p>
